title: A quotient of an adic completion killing a square-zero ideal of the kernel is again the completion of a finite type algebra
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a Noetherian ring A, an ideal I, a finite type A-algebra B, and a surjection B-hat -> C with kernel J, and assumes J/J^2 is annihilated by I^c for some c >= 0; it concludes that C is isomorphic to the completion of a finite type A-algebra (source lines 32036-32043). The proof is a long chain of reductions rather than a single citation. It first uses that B-hat is Noetherian to make J finitely generated, then deduces from an idempotent criterion that C_f = ((B-hat)_f)_e for some idempotent e, and uses a gluing lemma to find a complementary surjection B-hat -> C' such that B-hat -> C x C' becomes an isomorphism after inverting any f in I (proof lines 32046-32060). Choosing generators f_1, ..., f_r of I, the proof exhibits the object (C x C', B_{f_i}, alpha_i, alpha_{ij}) of the gluing category Glue(B -> B-hat, f_1, ..., f_r), for which it states that the verification of conditions (1)(a) and (1)(b) is omitted (proof lines 32062-32074). Because B -> B-hat is flat and induces an isomorphism on B/IB, the equivalence proposition and the formal gluing remark apply, giving that C x C' is isomorphic to D tensor_B B-hat for some finite B-algebra D (proof lines 32075-32081). The rest is a Hensel-type lifting argument: the idempotent of D/ID corresponding to the factor C/IC is lifted after an etale base change B -> B' trivial modulo I, using that the pair (C x C', IC x IC') is henselian since C x C' is I-adically complete, and the henselian-pair criterion lets B -> C x C' factor through B'; replacing B by B' and D by D' splits D = D_e x D_{1-e} into a product of finite type A-algebras whose completions are C and C' (proof lines 32082-32096). The gluing formalism, the etale idempotent lifting and the Hensel pair argument are independent research-level content.
